questions.question: In `See plans`, what is `href="/plans"`?
options: An attribute in the opening tag
questions.explanation: Attributes are name="value" pairs written inside the opening tag that add information to the element.

questions.question: In a CSS rule `.price { color: green; }`, which part is the property?
questions.explanation: .price is the selector, color is the property, and green is the value. Together color: green; is one declaration.

questions.question: You set `width: 200px` on a plain `<span>` and nothing changes. Why?
options: Spans cannot be styled with CSS
px is not a valid unit for width
A span is inline by default, and width has no effect on inline elements
questions.explanation: Inline elements are only as wide as their content and ignore width, height and vertical margins. Changing display to block or inline-block makes width apply.

questions.question: Why is `rem` usually preferred over `px` for font sizes?
options: rem is the only unit that works in every browser
rem scales with the root font size, so a user's larger default font setting enlarges text everywhere
rem values are always smaller than px values
px cannot be used for fonts
questions.explanation: 1rem equals the root font size (16px by default). If the user raises that default, rem-based text grows with it, which helps readability and accessibility.
